learningObjectives.title: Orbital motion, natural and artificial satellites

questions.q: Which object is at the centre of our solar system?
questions.explain: The Sun sits at the centre of the solar system, with the planets orbiting it.

questions.q: What name is given to a natural satellite that orbits a planet?
questions.explain: Moons are natural satellites that orbit planets.

questions.q: Our Sun formed from a cloud of dust and gas known as a:
questions.explain: The Sun formed from a nebula, a cloud of dust and gas pulled together by gravity.

questions.q: Our solar system is located within which galaxy?
questions.explain: The Sun is one of many billions of stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: What provides the force that keeps a planet in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explain: Gravity provides the centripetal force that keeps planets in orbit around the Sun.

questions.q: How long does a geostationary satellite take to complete one orbit of the Earth?
questions.explain: A geostationary satellite orbits once every 24 hours so it stays above the same point on Earth.

questions.q: Red-shift is a shift in the observed light from a galaxy towards:
questions.explain: Red-shift is an increase in observed wavelength towards the red end of the spectrum.

questions.q: According to the Big Bang theory, the universe began as a region that was:
questions.explain: The Big Bang theory states the universe began from a tiny, hot, dense region and has been expanding ever since.

questions.q: An object moving in a circular orbit at a constant speed is still accelerating because:
options: Its direction of motion is continually changing
questions.explain: Velocity has direction, so a continually changing direction means the velocity changes and the object accelerates.

questions.q: For an object to remain in a stable circular orbit, if its speed increases then the radius of the orbit must:
questions.explain: For a stable orbit a faster speed requires a smaller orbital radius.

questions.q: Compared with planets far from the Sun, planets that orbit closer to the Sun travel at:
questions.explain: Objects in smaller orbits must move faster to stay in a stable orbit.

questions.q: In which direction does the resultant force act on a satellite in a circular orbit?
options: Towards the centre of the orbit
Away from the centre of the orbit
Opposite to its direction of motion
questions.explain: The resultant (centripetal) force always acts towards the centre of the circular orbit.

questions.q: The observation that light from distant galaxies is red-shifted provides evidence that:
questions.explain: Galaxies moving away from us cause red-shift, which is evidence that the universe is expanding.

questions.q: Observations show that the more distant a galaxy is, the greater its red-shift. This suggests that more distant galaxies are:
questions.explain: Greater red-shift for more distant galaxies shows they are receding at greater speeds.

questions.q: Red-shift occurs because a galaxy is moving away from us, which causes the observed wavelength of its light to:
questions.explain: Motion away from the observer stretches the light, increasing its observed wavelength.

questions.q: Which observation is the main piece of evidence supporting the Big Bang theory?
options: Red-shift of light from distant galaxies
questions.explain: The red-shift of distant galaxies shows the universe is expanding, supporting the Big Bang theory.

questions.q: A satellite is moved from a low orbit to a higher orbit around the Earth. To stay in a stable orbit its speed must:
questions.explain: A larger orbital radius requires a slower orbital speed for a stable orbit.

questions.q: Light from a distant galaxy is observed to have a longer wavelength than expected. This tells us the galaxy is:
questions.explain: A longer observed wavelength (red-shift) indicates the galaxy is receding from Earth.

questions.q: A communications satellite must stay directly above the same point on the Earth's surface. Which orbit should it use?
questions.explain: A geostationary orbit has a 24-hour period, so the satellite stays above the same point on Earth.

questions.q: A comet moves in a highly elliptical orbit around the Sun. Its speed is greatest when it is:
questions.explain: In an elliptical orbit the object travels fastest when it is nearest the Sun, where gravity is strongest.
